title: Optimizing Cross-Service Financial Integration
business: A fintech firm managing a monorepo with separate micro-services for ledgering, authentication, and reporting.
problem: As the codebase grew, developers faced excessive build times because every minor change to a shared utility library triggered a full rebuild of all dependent services, leading to CI bottlenecks and developer frustration.
solution: By leveraging the Nx project graph, the team can map dependencies between services and libraries. Nx uses this graph to identify only the 'affected' projects when code changes, and its task execution engine caches results to skip redundant builds for unchanged modules.
steps: Define clear project boundaries using Nx configuration to isolate service logic from shared utilities.
Generate project-specific tasks using Nx generators to ensure consistent build and test configurations.
Analyze the project graph to visualize how the ledgering service depends on shared authentication modules.
Execute builds using the affected command to restrict task execution to only those projects impacted by the current commit.
Enable local caching to store task outputs, allowing subsequent runs to retrieve results instantly if inputs remain unchanged.
outcome: Developers experience significantly faster local feedback loops and reduced CI wait times, as the system intelligently avoids re-processing unaffected services.
limitation: The primary tradeoff is the overhead of maintaining accurate dependency metadata within the project graph. If developers manually bypass Nx to create hidden dependencies, the cache may return stale results, which can be verified by inspecting the graph output or clearing the cache explicitly.
